summary: Root delivery design for the 2,475,712,512-byte donor system.apfs without Android partitions. Host arithmetic on existing records of this S24 (runtime device-tree facts, NAT-068 loader and kernel logs) and on the loader/kernel sources. Findings: the loader caps the kernel's RAM window at 512 MiB while the device tree offers a free contiguous 4908 MiB gap once touching memory nodes are merged; the NAT-068 kernel ran with 4 KiB pages (131072 pages = 512 MiB) because arm_init selects 16 KiB only above 1 GiB; the loader's MMU-off clear (75 MB/s) would take 68 s for the big window; and three independent clocks bound a run (57 s software deadline reset = planned exit to Download Mode, 83 s hardware watchdog = SEC_UPLOAD failsafe, kernel timed return untested). Recommendation: loader-staged root over a new bulk-OUT endpoint into an enlarged window, bounded receive phase, small clear; first run with no transfer (NAT-075). Child tasks NAT-074..078 registered with acceptance criteria.
evidence_category: source-review / host arithmetic. Nothing ran on the S24 for this task. Transfer rates other than the donor's 28 MB/s figure are assumptions and are labelled so in the document. The iOS working set, 16 KiB-page boot, skipping the full clear, and the effect of a watchdog pet on this SoC are unmeasured.

acceptance.1_ram_budget: Met. Section 2 of the document and budget.json: 8033 MiB DRAM in 7 nodes, merged high region 6144 MiB, free gap 0x8cb800000-0x9fe400000 = 4908 MiB; replay of the loader's choose_window rule on the same facts reproduces the observed NAT-068 window (0x9de400000, 512 MiB); kernel page count 131072 = 512 MiB at 4 KiB. The root size is measured (IOS-010); the working-set margins are labelled estimates.
acceptance.2_options_with_time_and_failure_modes: Met. Section 4 compares A1 control-OUT, A2 bulk-OUT, B kernel USB block device and C smaller root for what must be written, host-testability and failure mode; section 3 gives the transfer-time table (assumed rates labelled) against the three measured/recorded bounds. The watchdog bound is taken from NAT-019/020/044/046 records; NAT-071 is not yet done and its kernel-side keepalive is named as a separate requirement.
acceptance.3_recommendation_and_first_tasks: Met. Section 5: one recommendation, NAT-074..NAT-078 with acceptance criteria, exact loader/ADT/boot-arg changes. No option uses an Android partition.

corrections_made_during_review: First draft attributed the +83.9 s reset in NAT-068 to the hardware watchdog and said the watchdog leads to Download Mode. The run records (NAT-044/046/058/068) show the software deadline reset ended those runs and that a watchdog reset gives SEC_UPLOAD; section 3 was rewritten.
Removed three figures that had no source in the repository (trial compression ratios, a /System uncompressed size, a '13 s to PID 1' offset) and a made-up RAMDisk address.

commands.result: OK: planning views match the current registry

limits: Rates for bulk-OUT and control-OUT are assumptions except the donor's 28 MB/s figure (another device and controller).
Whether the kernel boots with a 4908 MiB window and 16 KiB pages, whether skipping the full clear is safe, and whether the watchdog pet reloads the counter on this SoC are open until NAT-075.
The iOS working set against the 2427 MiB margin is not measured.
The 120 MiB kernel allowance is an estimate scaled from 81 MiB wired at 512 MiB.
The constant of the NAT-044 deadline in the NAT-067 image was not re-derived; the document uses the 57.1-57.2 s measured after enumeration.
